name: Soomaa National Park
blurb: Raised bogs, floodplain meadows and the spring flood Estonians call the fifth season.

tip.title: Skip the fifth season
tip.text: Spring floods water the meadows and forest edges. Set Spring flood to -100% and watch the sedges and willows, then the beavers, deer and predators that rely on them.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Bog moss that builds the wet peat of raised bogs such as Kuresoo, the best-known bog in the park.

nodes.name: Floodplain sedges & grasses
nodes.desc: Sedges of the riverside meadows that spend each spring under floodwater and feed many grazers.
Waterside trees and shrubs; willow is a staple food and building material for beavers.
Grazer of open ground that lynx turn to when roe deer are scarce.
Dabbling duck of flooded meadows and rivers that eats plant matter and small invertebrates.
Eats waterside plants and the bark and shoots of willow, aspen and birch. Its dams create wetland habitat for otters and others.
One of the most numerous large mammals in the park. An omnivore that roots for plants and small animals.

nodes.name: Roe deer
nodes.desc: A numerous browser of shoots and herbs, and the preferred prey of lynx in Estonia.

nodes.name: Elk (moose)
nodes.desc: Large browser of willow and pine twigs, and one of the park's most numerous big mammals.
Breeds and gathers on the bogs and floodplain; about a thousand gather here in autumn. Eats plants, voles and other small animals.
Hunts along rivers and beaver wetlands. Recorded eating ducks, frogs and snakes.
Raptor of forest edges and meadows that hunts voles, hares and other small animals.
Generalist hunter of voles, hares and ducks that also scavenges carcasses.
Ambush hunter. In Estonia roe deer are its main prey, with hares, beavers and foxes taken too.

nodes.name: Grey wolf
nodes.desc: Pack hunter of moose, roe deer and wild boar, and a top predator of the forest.
Omnivore that takes young deer and moose, beavers and carrion as well as plant foods.

nodes.name: Snowmelt & winter
nodes.desc: Winter snow and ice that melt into the yearly flood and shape how easily deer and moose can feed.

nodes.name: Peat & bog
nodes.desc: Wet raised-bog peat and swamp-forest soils that anchor mosses and trees.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Summer light that drives growth of meadow plants and trees.
Fungi and microbes that break down dead plants and carcasses into nutrients.

story: Soomaa National Park is situated in south-western Estonia. Created in 1993, it protects 390 square kilometres of large raised bogs, floodplain grasslands, paludified forests, and meandering rivers. Steep-sloped raised bogs stand as islands during spring floods.
matters: The park is the largest intact peat bog system in Europe preserved as wilderness. It is a home and breeding area for several mammal species that are very rare or extinct in other parts of Europe.
